request.system:
You are an HR investigation assistant. Using the
case folder, draft the investigation report for the hearing
manager: a summary of the evidence, a finding on the
allegation (substantiated, partly substantiated or not
substantiated) on the balance of probabilities, and a
recommended outcome. Under 400 words.

Case ER-2027-0907, Hartwell UK.
Allegation: That on 11 occasions between August 4 and August 27, 2027 you recorded call-outs at Leeds station as attended when you did not attend, and claimed the call-out payment for each.

[E01] Station duty manager (client), to Hartwell UK
From Sunita Barlow, station duty manager, September 6, 2027. Our access-control system shows no entry by your technician G. Whitlock on 11 nights in August when your call-out report says he attended. Please investigate and confirm whether these call-outs will be credited to us.

[E02] Hartwell UK call-out report, August 2027
Technician HW-032518 G. Whitlock. Call-outs recorded as attended at Leeds station: Aug 4 (CO-27-0811), Aug 5 (CO-27-0818), Aug 10 (CO-27-0842), Aug 12 (CO-27-0851), Aug 13 (CO-27-0857), Aug 16 (CO-27-0866), Aug 17 (CO-27-0871), Aug 19 (CO-27-0880), Aug 20 (CO-27-0884), Aug 22 (CO-27-0893), Aug 27 (CO-27-0912). Call-out payment 58 pounds each, 638 pounds in total.

[E03] Station access-control export (client), Gates 1 and 3
Badge HW-032518, August 1 to 31, 2027. Entries recorded on Aug 2, Aug 3, Aug 24, Aug 25, Aug 30 and Aug 31. No entry recorded on Aug 4, 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 20, 22 or 27. The export lists events only for readers that were online.

[E04] Investigation meeting with Gary Whitlock, Sept 14, 2027
GW said he attended every one of the 11 call-outs. Gate 3, the staff gate, was not reading badges for about two weeks in the middle of August, so on those nights he used the side door by the parcel office with the contractor key, which does not log. On August 4 he signed the platform office book. On August 5 the station's night supervisor let him in through Gate 1 on her own badge; he did not know her name. On August 27 the lift alarm had cleared by the time he arrived; he checked the lift panel from the car park level and reset the call on his handset without going into the station. He said "I've never claimed for a job I didn't go to."

[E05] Statement of Ian Kershaw, technician, Sept 15, 2027
Gate 3 was down for about two weeks in August. We all used the side door by the parcel office with the contractor key. I was with Gary on one of the lift jobs, the 17th I think. I don't know about the other nights.

[E06] Statement of Sunita Barlow, station duty manager, Sept 16, 2027
I work nights one week in three. I was on duty on August 4, 5 and 6 and August 25, 26 and 27. I did not see the Hartwell technician on any of those nights, but I am not always on the concourse. I was not told that Gate 3 was faulty.

[E07] Hartwell facilities helpdesk ticket FM-27-5521
Leeds station, Gate 3 staff reader not reading badges. Opened August 9, 2027 07:12. Closed August 23, 2027 15:40, controller replaced.

[E08] Platform office sign-in book, August 2027 (photo, transcribed)
Contractor entries for Hartwell: Aug 4, 23:05, "G Whitlock, Hartwell, lift 2". No Hartwell entry on Aug 5 or Aug 27.

[E09] HartwellOne record extract, added to the folder by the HR suite
Service since March 5, 2018. No live warnings. Grievance raised March 2027 about the allocation of weekend overtime, not upheld. Sickness absence June 7 to 11, 2027, back pain.

[E10] Hartwell UK call-out policy v3, section 4
A call-out payment is due when the technician attends the site in response to a call-out, including where the fault has cleared on arrival. The site includes the car park and plant areas of the contract.

content.text:
INVESTIGATION REPORT: Case ER-2027-0907

**Allegation:** That on 11 occasions between Aug 4 and Aug 27, 2027 Mr Whitlock recorded call-outs at Leeds station as attended when he did not, and claimed the payment for each (£638 in total).

**Summary of the evidence**

The client's access-control export (E03) shows no badge entry for Mr Whitlock on any of the 11 dates. That export covers only readers that were online. Gate 3 was faulty from August 9 to 23 (E07), so it cannot support an absence finding for the dates falling in that window: Aug 10, 12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 22. Mr Kershaw (E05) confirms the fault and the side-door practice, and was with Mr Whitlock on one lift job, probably the 17th.

The remaining dates are Aug 4, 5 and 27. Gate 3 was working on Aug 4 and 5 and was repaired before Aug 27, so the fault does not explain the lack of entries on those dates. Each has its own evidence:

- **Aug 4:** The sign-in book (E08) records Mr Whitlock at 23:05, which supports attendance and is independent of the badge system. Ms Barlow (E06) did not see him but was not always on the concourse.
- **Aug 5:** No book entry, no badge entry, and no corroboration. Mr Whitlock says an unnamed night supervisor admitted him on her own badge. Ms Barlow was on duty that night and does not mention doing so. This account has not been tested with her.
- **Aug 27:** No book entry or badge entry. Mr Whitlock says he checked the lift from car park level without entering. Under policy section 4 (E10) that is attendance, as the car park is part of the site and a cleared fault does not remove entitlement. This depends on his account alone and is plausible, but it is uncorroborated.

Mr Whitlock has 9 years' service and no live warnings (E09). His prior grievance and sickness record carry no weight on this allegation.

**Finding: Not substantiated** on the balance of probabilities.

For 8 dates the client's evidence is unreliable because of the Gate 3 fault. For Aug 4 there is positive evidence of attendance. For Aug 5 and 27 the evidence is thin, but the explanations are consistent with the documented facts and the policy, and there is no evidence of falsification. The burden rests with the company.

**Recommended outcome**

1. No disciplinary action; the 11 payments stand.
2. Before the hearing, put Mr Whitlock's Aug 5 account to Ms Barlow and ask the station to identify the night supervisor. If that account is disproved, the finding on Aug 5 should be revisited.
3. Reply to the client confirming the Gate 3 fault, and ask for CCTV or other logs for Aug 5 and 27 if available.
4. Management should note that the contractor key does not log, and that the side-door practice left no record of attendance. Technicians should be reminded to sign the contractor book when readers are down.

request.system:
You prepare the case file for a human investigator
and hearing manager, who will make every finding and decide
every outcome. You never do either.
From the case folder, write:
1. chronology: dated events, each with the item ID and a
   short quote (under 20 words) copied word for word from
   that item; one entry per date, not one per item;
2. by_point: for each point in dispute, what each source
   says, as word-for-word quotes, one item ID per quote;
3. open_questions: questions nobody has asked yet;
4. not_relied_on: IDs of items outside the allegation.
Do not find, weigh, rate credibility, say what is likely or
recommend an outcome. Do not repeat anything about earlier
grievances, health, sickness, leave or union matters.
Reply with JSON only:
{"chronology": [{"date": "", "event": "", "item": "",
"quote": ""}], "by_point": [{"point": "", "sources":
[{"item": "", "quote": ""}]}], "open_questions": [""],
"not_relied_on": [""]}

open_questions: Who was the night supervisor on duty on August 5, and has she been asked about letting Whitlock in via Gate 1?
Does the Gate 1 log for August 5 show a badge entry by the supervisor around the time of CO-27-0818?
What are the call-out times and fault details for each of the 11 call-outs, and what do the handset records show for Whitlock's location or activity?
Do Whitlock's handset records for August 27 show a reset of the call and from where, and are there car park or lift-panel logs or CCTV for that night?
Is there CCTV of the side door by the parcel office, or any contractor key issue or usage record?
Does the helpdesk ticket record that Whitlock or any technician reported the Gate 3 fault, and why does the first ticket date (August 9) fall after the first listed call-out (August 4)?
Was Gate 3 working or not on the nights of August 4 to 8, before the ticket was opened?

What were the Gate 1 and Gate 3 readings on the nights outside the 11, and does Whitlock's badge pattern (entries on Aug 2, 3, 24, 25, 30, 31) say anything about which gate he used when it was working?
Did other technicians claim call-outs at Leeds station during the Gate 3 outage, and do their badge records show the same gaps?
Has Kershaw been asked which lift job he attended with Whitlock on or about the 17th, and does it match CO-27-0871?
Are there other sign-in books or logs (for example, at the parcel office or the lift plant room) for the 11 dates?
Were the call-out payments for these 11 call-outs actually paid, and has the client been invoiced for them?
Has the client been asked to check whether it holds any other records for the 11 nights, such as CCTV or Gate 1 logs?
What did Whitlock record on the call-out reports as the work done on each date, and were there follow-up or confirming calls from the client?
